regime.title: eIDAS (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by 2024/1183): qualified electronic ledgers and qualified electronic time stamps
regime.determination_by: a supervisory body, and the courts

source.citation: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183
source.note: eur-lex.europa.eu and etsi.org were unreachable when this map was written; article content follows docs/security/PROVENANCE_INTEROP.md §1.1 and is unverified; no sub-paragraph letters are used; requirement text is our paraphrase

rows.requirement: An electronic ledger is not denied legal effect solely for being electronic or for not being a qualified electronic ledger.
rows.mechanism: None; this is a legal effect, not a mechanism.
rows.reason: A legal effect a court applies to any ledger; it requires no mechanism and SecuraCV claims none.

rows.requirement: Records in a qualified electronic ledger are presumed to be uniquely and accurately ordered and intact.
rows.mechanism: SecuraCV is not a qualified electronic ledger.
rows.reason: The presumption attaches only to qualified electronic ledgers; SecuraCV is not one and seeks no qualification.

rows.requirement: A qualified electronic ledger is created by one or more qualified trust service providers.
rows.mechanism: No qualified trust service provider operates a SecuraCV ledger.
rows.reason: Qualification needs a supervised qualified trust service provider and a conformity assessment — a centralized regime absorbed only as a projection (tension 8).

rows.requirement: Records are in unique, accurate chronological order.
rows.mechanism: Each entry hashes its predecessor; the chain fails verification when reordered.

rows.requirement: The integrity of records is protected and any change is detectable.
rows.mechanism: An external signed high-water mark fails closed on tail truncation, rollback or wipe.

rows.requirement: The origin of records is identifiable.
Records are in unique, accurate chronological order.
rows.mechanism: A Merkle tree and a signed checkpoint over every ledger.

rows.requirement: The integrity of records is protected and any change is detectable.

rows.clause: ETSI standards for qualified electronic ledgers
rows.requirement: Standards for qualified electronic ledgers set technical requirements.
rows.reason: No ETSI document for qualified electronic ledgers was identified or read; none is tracked against.

rows.requirement: A qualified electronic time stamp carries a presumption of accurate date and time and of integrity.
rows.mechanism: A TSA's qualification is the operator's declaration in the anchor policy (src/anchor_policy.rs:10-11).
rows.operator_action: Point one of the two TSAs at a qualified TSA the operator checked on the trusted list, and record why.

rows.requirement: Time-stamp evidence does not rest on one authority.
rows.mechanism: The anchor policy requires a minimum number of distinct TSAs.
